result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-019.md for WF02-REQ-019 (profile capture as a resumable step-by-step form, consent gate, optional-field rule) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-019, commit 04ea290. Scope test: FRONTEND-DEV/BACKEND-DEV's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts + drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql, domain/{profile,onboarding}.ts new, handlers/profile.ts new, handlers/start.ts modified, i18n additions, index.ts) is real behavioral surface (3 new commands, 2 new generic listeners, 4 new callback handlers, a real migration) -- full Steps 3b/4 apply, not a docs-only skip.

Read apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts, domain/onboarding.ts, handlers/profile.ts, handlers/start.ts (as modified for the zero-active-chapters rework, commit 244c9e1), docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md, docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md, the existing profile.test.ts/onboarding.test.ts (pure-function coverage already in place), the real i18n/en.ts and ru.ts profile catalog blocks (quoted verbatim in the spec, not guessed), the real drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql migration file, and index.ts's actual registration lines, before writing a single case -- every fixture id, tg_id, and expected string in the spec is grounded in a file I actually opened, not inferred from the design doc's prose alone.

Each of the 6 acceptance criteria has at least one concrete, judgment-free verification case (exact fixture SQL, exact dispatch calls or exact grep/read commands, exact expected values):
- AC1 (kill+restart mid-form resumes at the next unanswered field, first answers preserved): the one case in this spec built around a REAL process kill+restart rather than same-process simulation, per this run's explicit instruction. Two separate `npx tsx` invocations (apps/bot/scratch-verify-req019-ac1-phase1.ts / -phase2.ts) as two genuinely separate OS processes with no shared import or memory of any kind -- phase 1 answers 3 required fields, prints its own PID, then hangs on an unresolved promise (never calls process.exit itself); TEST-RUNNER is instructed to poll for the PID line then forcibly kill that exact process (Stop-Process -Force / kill -9) and confirm it is actually gone before starting phase 2. Phase 2 is a fresh process reading only Postgres, dispatching the 4th answer, and the pass condition requires it resume at field 4 (not re-ask fields 1-3) and correctly advance to field 5 afterward, with all three pre-kill answers read back unchanged.
- AC2 (skip every optional field completes the profile): unit-test re-run plus 5 live Skip dispatches (mixed button-text-match for phone, callback-pattern for the other four) against a real Postgres row, checking all five *_skipped columns land true with value columns untouched, the guided flow announces completion after the fifth skip, and a follow-up /profile renders the view (not a 6th prompt).
- AC3 (declining consent -> zero profiles rows, plain block not error): live /start then /profile dispatch by a never-consented user, checking both replies are the plain consent.prompt string and profiles stays at count 0 throughout.
- AC4 (already-complete profile asked no question on second pass -- design section 8.3's stated interim substitute, since REQ-020 doesn't exist): unit-test re-run plus two consecutive live /profile dispatches against a genuinely complete (all-real-values, not all-skips) profile, searching captured for all eleven prompt strings by name and requiring zero matches on either pass.
- AC5 (phone/email entered, error path logs neither value): live dispatch of a malformed email against a fixture that already has a real phone value stored, redirecting the harness process's own stdout/stderr to files and grepping those files (not the mocked Telegram captures) for both the phone value and the rejected email string, requiring zero matches in either.
- AC6 (email accepted absent, format-validated only when supplied): unit-test re-run plus a live Skip dispatch (proving the format check path is never invoked at all, not merely that it happens to pass) and a live malformed-then-corrected typed-answer sequence.

Per this run's explicit instruction, restated SECURITY-REVIEWER's Step 2c adversarial scenarios (handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-02c-security-reviewer.json) as this spec's own AC-mapped cases rather than a carried-over reference: field-mismatch and stale-replay (SECURITY-REVIEWER's scenarios 1/2) are mapped to a new AC1b -- my own judgment call, departing from the security handoff's own suggested AC3 mapping, since neither scenario touches the consent gate at all; both are actually about whether a forged/stale profile-step callback can desync from the currently-derived field, which is AC1's resumability-integrity property under adversarial input, not AC3's consent property. Chapter-but-no-consent and forged-skip-while-unconsented (scenarios 3/4) are mapped to a new AC3b, which does sit squarely on the consent gate. All four are restated with their own fresh fixtures and dispatches, not merely referenced.

Also included: AC-schema (reads the real drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql and diffs its 11 statements against REQ-019-schema.md section 5's predicted list verbatim) and AC-catalog (i18n key-set parity across types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts's profile blocks, plus index.ts's actual command/listener/callback registration lines) as mechanical, non-dispatch checks.

Noted ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement explicitly in the spec's own execution-note section for TEST-RUNNER, and flagged that the live-dispatch harness scripts must not run concurrently with any other DB-backed vitest file against the same scratch Postgres. ISS-0013 (no CI Postgres) is referenced as informational context only, per this run's instruction not to attempt to fix either gap.

Gap found in existing unit tests: none that blocks this spec -- profile.test.ts and onboarding.test.ts correctly cover every pure-function rule table cell, but (as expected and as those files' own header comments already state) neither exercises a real handler, a real Postgres row, or -- for AC1 specifically -- a genuinely separate process; that is exactly the gap this spec's live cases are designed to close. No design or implementation defect was found while doing this reading -- nothing new to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
